title: Broad Immunity of AB-phages treated Acinetobacter baumannii Implications for Phage Therapy Strategies
content: Phage therapy is increasingly considered a viable alternative to combat multi-drug-resistant bacteria, including Acinetobacter baumannii (AB), a significant nosocomial pathogen. In this study, an AB isolate, designated ABU-3, was found susceptible to three distinct AB-phages, termed AB-phage 22, 27, and 32. The ABU-3 isolate was treated with these phages at various multiplicities of infection (MOI) to identify the MOI necessary to completely eliminate ABU-3, referred to as the "MOI clearance value." Results showed that the MOI clearance values for AB-phage 22, 27, and 32 were 10, 100, and 10, respectively. Additionally, colonies of ABU-3 that survived treatment with each AB-phage at lower MOIs were isolated and assessed for susceptibility or resistance to all three phages. The results indicated that ABU-3 became resistant to AB-phage 27 but remained susceptible to AB-phages 22 and 32 at titers similar to the original ABU-3 control. ABU-3 also developed complete resistance to AB-phage 22 but remained susceptible to AB-phages 27 and 32, though at a 2-log lower MOI compared to the original ABU-3. In contrast, AB-phage 32-resistant ABU-3 exhibited complete resistance to all three AB-phages. These findings highlight a potential complication in phage therapy, underscoring the importance of carefully managing MOI to prevent resistance. The varying immunity profiles of AB-phage-treated AB isolates under inappropriate MOI conditions could complicate phage therapy by promoting phage resistance. We propose prioritizing the MOI clearance value as a critical metric for effective phage therapy, particularly for multi-drug-resistant bacterial pathogens.
